_comment: Which demonstrations exist, and what each one needs running.
The stack grew to twelve stacks and about 10 GB, and almost none of it
is needed for any ONE demonstration. So the core stays up and everything
else is started on demand -- from the Demos page in GatewayAdmin, or from
`make demo-start`, both of which go through the same control plane.
A stack may appear in several demos, and that is the point: the edges
carry the EAM push and the store-and-forward road.
Nothing here reference-counts by hand -- the control plane reconciles
against the set of demos you have asked for, so stopping one demo cannot
take a stack out from under another one that is still running.
The CORE is not a demo and the page cannot stop it: the gateway serving
the button is in it, and a page that can kill its own gateway will, once,
in front of somebody. `make down` still stops everything, as always --
the command line keeps the big hammer, the page does not get one.
Each demo is titled after its own tab, and that pairing is the whole
navigation. `tab` names the tab a demo is shown on: the tab is DISABLED
until that demo is running, because a tab whose stacks are down renders
cards full of dashes and reads as broken rather than un-started. The key
is the vocabulary demo_guide.TAB_TOPICS uses and deliberately NOT a tab
index -- an index would couple this file to the order of Main's children,
which ia.container.tab keys by POSITION and which nothing would re-check
if it changed.
The ORDER of this list is the order the cards are drawn in, and it must
match the order of the tabs along the top -- a card third from the left
whose tab is first reads as two different navigations, and the eye tries
to pair them by position before it reads either label. That order lives
in demo_control.TAB_KEYS, and `make validate` cross-checks the two, since
either can be reordered on its own and the page still renders perfectly.
The page draws ONE ROW of demo_control.ACROSS (4) tiles: demos fill it
from the left, the rest are inert dotted slots with a '+', which is how
the page says more demonstrations are coming rather than implying the
current count is the product. Adding a demo here consumes a slot and
needs no layout change until the row is exactly full (it is, at four:
eam, store-forward, redundancy, sparkplug). A FIFTH needs both
demo_control.ACROSS and the repeater's basis in Demos/view.json moved
together, and validate fails until they are.

core.why: The front door, the gateway that hosts the console (and, on its redundant pair, the MQTT broker), and the control plane itself.

demos.title: EAM Demo
demos.blurb: Push a project from the hub to both edges and watch it land, without touching either of them.

demos.title: Store & Forward Demo
demos.blurb: An edge that keeps its data through an outage and hands it over afterwards -- over the Gateway Network and over MQTT.

demos.title: Redundancy Demo
demos.blurb: Two gateways behind one name. Fail the active half and watch the front door follow it.

demos.title: MQTT Demo
demos.blurb: Two Edge gateways with no Gateway Network: tags, alarms, acknowledgements and notifications reach the cloud over MQTT (Sparkplug B), and commands come back.
